CalMac Ferries: The Motorcyclist's Guide to Scottish Island Hopping

Caledonian MacBrayne — CalMac — operates the ferry network connecting mainland Scotland to its western islands. For motorcycle tourers, these ferries unlock some of the most spectacular and remote riding in Britain. Here's everything you need to know to book, board, and enjoy the crossing.

Key CalMac Routes for Motorcycle Tourers

  • Oban to Mull (Craignure): 45 minutes. Gateway to Mull's single-track roads and the onward ferry to Iona.
  • Ardrossan to Arran (Brodick): 55 minutes. Arran is "Scotland in miniature" — mountains, coast, and castles in a compact island.
  • Uig (Skye) to Tarbert (Harris): 1hr 40min. Access to the Outer Hebrides' machair roads and wild Atlantic coastline.
  • Mallaig to Armadale (Skye): 30 minutes. The scenic alternative to the Skye Bridge, approaching from the south.
  • Kennacraig to Islay: 2 hours. For whisky distillery touring on Islay and Jura.
  • Ullapool to Stornoway (Lewis): 2hr 45min. The main gateway to Lewis and Harris.

Booking Tips for Motorcyclists

CalMac treats motorcycles differently from cars, and understanding this saves money and stress:

  • Book early in summer: July and August sailings to popular islands (Skye, Mull, Arran) can sell out for vehicles weeks in advance. Foot passengers are rarely turned away, but motorcycle spaces are limited.
  • Book online at calmac.co.uk: Select "motorcycle" as your vehicle type. You'll be charged less than a car — typically 50-60% of the car fare.
  • Hopscotch tickets: CalMac's Hopscotch passes offer discounted multi-ferry tickets for island-hopping itineraries. These represent excellent value for motorcycle tourers visiting multiple islands.
  • Arrive 30 minutes before sailing: CalMac asks vehicles to check in 30 minutes before departure. Arrive earlier in peak season.

What to Expect on Board

CalMac ferries range from small open-deck vessels on minor routes to large roll-on, roll-off ships on major crossings. As a motorcyclist, you'll typically:

  • Queue in a dedicated motorcycle lane at the terminal
  • Board first or last (varies by vessel and route)
  • Park on the car deck — crew will direct you to a specific spot
  • Secure your bike on the side stand (some routes use chocks or tie-downs provided by crew)
  • Leave your helmet locked to your bike and head upstairs to the passenger deck
CalMac crew are experienced with motorcycles and will help you position and secure your bike. Don't be shy about asking for chocks or advice — they'd rather help than deal with a fallen bike mid-crossing.

Costs (2026 Approximate)

  • Oban to Mull: £12-18 (motorcycle + rider)
  • Ardrossan to Arran: £10-15
  • Uig to Tarbert: £20-28
  • Ullapool to Stornoway: £22-30
  • Hopscotch Island Rover: Various multi-trip discounts from £40-80

Tips for a Smooth Crossing

  • Put your bike in first gear and turn off the fuel tap (if applicable) — this prevents it rolling.
  • Attach a disc lock as extra security.
  • Take valuables and waterproofs with you upstairs — car decks can get spray in rough weather.
  • Check the weather forecast for your crossing. Rough seas can delay or cancel sailings. CalMac posts real-time updates on their app and website.
  • Use the crossing time to study your onward route — island roads are often single-track with limited signage.

Island Riding Essentials

Once you're on a Scottish island, riding is different from the mainland:

  • Single-track roads with passing places are the norm. Pull into the nearest passing place on your left to let oncoming traffic pass.
  • Fuel stations are limited — fill up at every opportunity.
  • Many islands have no mobile signal in large areas. Download offline maps before boarding.
  • Wildlife on roads is common — sheep, deer, and otters don't check for traffic.

CalMac ferries are an essential part of Scottish motorcycle touring. The crossings themselves are a highlight — standing on deck watching the islands grow closer while dolphins play in the bow wake is pure magic. faq.q: How much cheaper are CalMac motorcycle fares?
faq.a: Motorcycles are charged less than cars, typically 50 to 60% of the car fare. Book online at calmac.co.uk and select motorcycle as your vehicle type. Sample fares include Oban to Mull at £12 to £18, Ardrossan to Arran at £10 to £15 and Ullapool to Stornoway at £22 to £30 for a motorcycle and rider.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance?
faq.a: In July and August, sailings to popular islands such as Skye, Mull and Arran can sell out for vehicles weeks ahead. Foot passengers are rarely turned away, but motorcycle spaces are limited, so book early in summer. Outside peak season you have far more flexibility.

Hopscotch passes are CalMac's discounted multi-ferry tickets designed for island-hopping itineraries, with various options from around £40 to £80. They represent excellent value for motorcycle tourers visiting several islands, so if your route strings together multiple crossings, price up a Hopscotch against individual tickets.

faq.q: How are motorcycles secured on board?
faq.a: You queue in a dedicated motorcycle lane, board when directed and park where the crew position you on the car deck. Secure the bike on the side stand in first gear; on some routes crew provide chocks or tie-downs. CalMac crew are experienced with motorcycles, so ask for chocks or advice rather than risk a fallen bike mid-crossing.

faq.q: What should I prepare for island riding?
faq.a: Download offline maps before boarding, because many islands have large areas with no mobile signal and limited signage. Expect single-track roads with passing places: pull into the nearest one on your left to let oncoming traffic pass. Fuel stations are limited, so fill up at every opportunity, and watch for sheep, deer and otters on the roads.
